direction: Refine the globally depot-distance-scale-normalized generalized Clarke-Wright savings rule for L2a static merge: single vectorized pre-loop scoring using lam in [1.00,1.15] on d(i,j), mu in [0.08,0.15] radial asymmetry term |d(0,i)-d(0,j)|, plus a light dimensionless capacity-fill reward beta in [0.05,0.15] on clip((q_i+q_j)/Q,0,1) and an optional endpoint demand-balance term; strictly forbid per-pair (d0i+d0j) normalization.

operations.mechanism: Active template is cvrp_parallel_merge_static with postprocess 'none', and the archive is empty (solver_count=0), so the first stepping stone should reproduce the strongest verified L2a behavior in the KB rather than explore blind. KB method-cvrp-m2-l2a-generalized-savings gives the exact verified hook family (global scale mean(d[0,1:]), lam 1.00-1.15, mu 0.08-0.15, beta 0.05-0.15, one-shot vectorized scoring) with dev_24 = 16.1398 at 0.00% scale drift and hook median < 0.4 ms, i.e. large budget margin under the 25 ms cap. The anti-pattern entry forbids per-pair (d0i+d0j) normalization, which destroys far-customer radial ordering (degrades dev_24 to ~18.0). Postprocess stays 'none' to isolate the merge-construction layer's contribution; relocate_2opt can be re-attributed in a later round once this baseline is archived (KB notes this as the open question).

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Normalizing the generalized savings expression by a single global depot-distance scale mean(d(0,1..n)) — instead of the per-pair local ratio (d0i+d0j-dij)/(d0i+d0j) — preserves the radial priority of far-from-depot customers while keeping exact coordinate-scale invariance, so a lam/mu/beta-tuned one-shot vectorized scoring hook on cvrp_parallel_merge_static with postprocess_mode='none' will beat bare Clarke-Wright (16.2225) and CW+relocate+2opt (16.1549) on dev_hetero_24, reaching mean_tour_length <~16.15 within the 25 ms budget with zero timeout truncations.
